items.claim: attrs follows Calendar Versioning (CalVer).
items.label: supported
items.reason: The changelog and security policy explicitly state that versions follow Calendar Versioning.

items.claim: Setting the annotations before the build would have made `_transform_attrs` read them as auto-attribs declarations.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: `_transform_attrs` lives in src/attr/_make.py, which is not included in the shown files, so the auto-attribs reading behavior can't be checked.

items.claim: `_has_own_attribute` is implemented as `attrib_name in cls.__dict__`, checking only the class's own dict rather than its MRO.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: `_has_own_attribute` is defined in src/attr/_make.py, which is not shown.

items.claim: `@attr.s` is aliased as `@attr.attributes`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `s = attributes = attrs` makes `attr.attributes` an alias of the same decorator as `attr.s`.

items.claim: `make_class` applies the decorator as `_attrs(these=cls_dict, **attributes_arguments)(type_)`.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: `make_class`'s implementation is in the unshown src/attr/_make.py; only its stub signature is visible.

items.claim: `add_repr` calls `_make_repr_script`, which returns a source string and a globals dict.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: `add_repr` / `_make_repr_script` are in src/attr/_make.py, which is not shown.

items.claim: `Attribute` defines `__setattr__` to raise `FrozenInstanceError`.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: The `Attribute` class body (including any `__setattr__`) is in the unshown src/attr/_make.py.

items.claim: `Factory`'s `takes_self` parameter defaults to `False`.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: Only overloaded stubs for `Factory` are visible (which give no default); the runtime definition in src/attr/_make.py is not shown.

items.claim: The attrs `attrs` namespace is built on top of the `attr` logic internally.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The docs state the `attrs` namespace is built on top of `attr`, and the `attrs` submodules simply re-export from `attr`.

items.claim: `_ClassBuilder.__init__` puts `__attrs_attrs__` and `__attrs_props__` into the class dict.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: `_ClassBuilder.__init__` is defined in the unshown src/attr/_make.py.

items.claim: `_create_slots_class` walks the new class's dict, unwrapping classmethods, staticmethods and properties, and overwrites any closure cell whose contents are the old class.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: `_create_slots_class` is in src/attr/_make.py, which is not included.

items.claim: `FrozenInstanceError` is raised when a `frozen=True` class is modified.
items.label: supported
items.reason: Documentation and doctests show that setting an attribute on a frozen class raises `attrs.exceptions.FrozenInstanceError`.

items.claim: `astuple`'s `recurse` parameter defaults to `True`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `astuple`'s signature defines `recurse=True` as the default.

items.claim: Slotted classes do not have a `__dict__` and prevent adding new attributes at runtime that weren't defined in `__slots__`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The glossary states slotted classes have no `object.__dict__` and shows an AttributeError when setting an undeclared attribute.

items.claim: The attrs benchmark suite measures `__eq__`, `__hash__`, `asdict`, and `astuple`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The benchmark file contains test_eq_equal/test_eq_unequal, test_hash, test_asdict_complicated and test_astuple_complicated.

items.claim: `_generate_unique_filename` appends a counter when the candidate filename is already taken by different source.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: `_generate_unique_filename` is in the unshown src/attr/_make.py.

items.claim: `optional(validator)` allows the value to be `None` or satisfy the provided validator.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The documented example shows `optional(instance_of(int))` accepting `None` and otherwise enforcing the wrapped validator.

items.claim: `attrs.inspect` is documented as experimental and outside the project's backwards-compatibility guarantee.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The changelog introduces `attrs.inspect()` explicitly as "a new **experimental** way to inspect classes".

items.claim: `Converter(takes_self=True)` enables a converter function to be called as `fn(val, self)`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The Converter stub overload with `takes_self: Literal[True]` types the converter as `Callable[[In, AttrsInstance], Out]`, i.e. called as fn(val, self).

items.claim: The `field_transformer` hook receives the class being decorated and a list of `Attribute` objects.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The documented hook signature is `your_hook(cls: type, fields: list[attrs.Attribute]) -> list[attrs.Attribute]`.

items.claim: The `Converter` class can be configured with `takes_self` and `takes_field` parameters.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `attrs.Converter` accepts `takes_self` and `takes_field` keyword arguments per the stub and docs example.

items.claim: For a mandatory field with no factory and no converter, the alias is added to `args` as a bare positional parameter and `_assign('a', 'a', False)` returns `'self.a = a'`.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: The `__init__`-generation helpers (`_assign`, arg building) live in the unshown src/attr/_make.py.

items.claim: Annotations wrapped in `typing.ClassVar` are ignored by the attrs attribute collection process.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The docs state attrs skips members annotated with `typing.ClassVar` and the doctest shows the ClassVar member is ignored.

items.claim: The pre-commit `interrogate` hook ensures the `tests` directory maintains docstring coverage.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The interrogate pre-commit hook is run with the `tests` argument and configured with fail-under = 100.

items.claim: `converters.optional` returns `None` directly for `None` values without calling the wrapped converter.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The doctest shows `converters.optional(int)` yielding `C(x=None)` for `None`, which is only possible if `int` is not invoked on `None`.

items.claim: The tox `docs-watch` environment uses `watchfiles` to trigger rebuilds when source or documentation files change.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The `docs-watch` dependency group adds `watchfiles`, and CONTRIBUTING documents `tox run -e docs-watch` as watching for changes and rebuilding.

items.claim: `_determine_setters(frozen=False, slots=False, base_attr_map={})` returns `((), _assign, _assign_with_converter)` because `slots` is irrelevant when the class is not frozen.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: `_determine_setters` is defined in src/attr/_make.py, which is not shown.

items.claim: In Python, objects that compare equal must have the same hash.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The hashing docs state that two equal objects must have the same hash.

items.claim: Validators are attached to attributes using the `validator` parameter in `attrs.field()` or `attr.ib()`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: Both docs and the `attrib`/`field` stubs show a `validator` parameter used to attach validators.

items.claim: In `asdict`, when `filter` is None the per-field skip check does not fire and when `value_serializer` is None the serializer hook does not run.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `asdict` guards both hooks with `if filter is not None and not filter(a, v): continue` and `if value_serializer is not None:`.

items.claim: `_compile_and_eval()` compiles the generated script into bytecode.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: `_compile_and_eval()` lives in `src/attr/_make.py`, which is not shown in the provided excerpt.

items.claim: The generated `__setattr__` looks the field up in a dict and, if the hook is a generator function, drives it around the assignment.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: The changelog mentions generator `on_setattr` hooks, but the generated `__setattr__` code is in the unshown src/attr/_make.py.

items.claim: When a type annotation is present, it is stored in `Attribute.type`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The doctest shows `fields(C).x.type` returning `<class 'int'>` for an annotated attribute, and `Attribute.type` exists in the stub.

items.claim: `_is_class_var` stringifies the annotation, strips surrounding quotes, and tests `annot.startswith(_CLASSVAR_PREFIXES)`.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: `_is_class_var` is implemented in the unshown src/attr/_make.py; the changelog only notes the feature.

items.claim: `_transform_attrs` ensures no mandatory attributes follow attributes with default values.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: The behavior is documented, but `_transform_attrs` itself is defined in `src/attr/_make.py`, which is not shown, so the attribution to that function cannot be checked.

items.claim: `_collect_base_attrs_broken` walks the MRO forward instead of reversed, keeps attributes already marked `inherited`, and mutates the `taken_attr_names` set it was given.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: `_collect_base_attrs_broken` is in src/attr/_make.py, which is not shown.

items.claim: attrs classes automatically generate `__match_args__` based on the attribute order to support structural pattern matching.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The changelog documents that `__match_args__` are generated to support structural pattern matching, controlled by the `match_args` argument.

items.claim: The generated `__repr__` renders the class name from `self.__class__.__qualname__`.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: The `__repr__` generation code resides in the unshown src/attr/_make.py.

items.claim: When no `__attrs_pre_init__` exists, `_ClassBuilder.__init__` makes no `inspect.signature` call and leaves the hook flags False.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: `_ClassBuilder.__init__` and its `__attrs_pre_init__` detection are in the unshown src/attr/_make.py.

items.claim: NFKC normalization is the same normalization the Python parser applies to identifiers.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: This is a statement about CPython's identifier handling, not about anything in the shown repository code.

items.claim: `attrs` performs its work at class definition time via code generation, minimizing runtime impact at instantiation.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The docs state everything happens once at class definition via generated methods with no runtime overhead at instantiation.

items.claim: `evolve` works with frozen classes because it calls the constructor rather than mutating the instance.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The API docs explicitly say `evolve` creates a new instance using `__init__`, and the examples use it on frozen classes.

items.claim: `converters.default_if_none` replaces `None` values with a static default value or the result of a factory function.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The stub shows `default_if_none` overloads taking either a static `default` value or a `factory` callable.

items.claim: The modern attrs API was introduced in version 20.1.0.
items.label: supported
items.reason: docs/names.md states the modern (`define`/`field`) APIs were added in attrs 20.1.0.

items.claim: `_transform_attrs` returns `_Attributes(AttrsClass(attrs), base_attrs, base_attr_map)`.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: `_transform_attrs`'s return value is defined in the unshown src/attr/_make.py.

items.claim: `has` checks for the presence of the `__attrs_attrs__` attribute on the class.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `has()` reads `getattr(cls, "__attrs_attrs__", None)` (falling back to the generic base) to decide.

items.claim: `make_class` creates the class with `types.new_class(name, bases, {}, lambda ns: ns.update(body))`.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: `make_class` lives in `src/attr/_make.py`, which is not shown, so its use of `types.new_class` cannot be checked.

items.claim: If `cache_hash=True` is passed to `@define`, the hash value is computed once and stored on the instance.
items.label: supported
items.reason: Docs and changelog describe `cache_hash=True` as computing the hash once and storing it on the object.

items.claim: In auto_attribs mode, a class-body value that is not a `_CountingAttr` is wrapped by `attrib(a)` as a default.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: The auto_attribs collection logic is in the unshown `src/attr/_make.py`.

items.claim: The `benchmark` dependency group includes `pytest-codspeed` and `pytest-xdist`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The `benchmark` dependency group lists `pytest-codspeed` and `pytest-xdist[psutil]`.

items.claim: When fields have no types, the generated init `annotations` dict is just `{'return': None}` because the annotation step requires `a.type` to be non-None.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: The init-script annotation generation lives in the unshown `_make.py`; the docs only show an annotated example.

items.claim: The keyword-only decision in `attrs` is gated on `kw_only` being truthy before `force_kw_only` applies.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: The `kw_only`/`force_kw_only` handling is inside the unshown `_make.py`.

items.claim: `build_class` sets `__attrs_base_of_slotted__ = weakref.ref(cls)` on the original class when building a slotted class.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: `build_class` and the slotted-class machinery are in the unshown `_make.py`.

items.claim: The `auto_exc` parameter defaults to `False` in legacy `attr.s` and `True` in modern `attrs.define`.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: The documented `attr.s` signature shows `auto_exc=False`, but `attrs.define`'s default lives in src/attr/_next_gen.py, whose contents are not shown.

items.claim: `_make_init_script` merges the defining module's entire `__dict__` into the generated globals if the module is importable.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: `_make_init_script` is defined in the unshown `_make.py`.

items.claim: In the non-annotated path, attrs sorts the class body fields by the `_CountingAttr` counter.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: Attribute collection/counter sorting happens in the unshown `_make.py`.

items.claim: In `_transform_attrs`, each annotated name is looked up with `a = cd.get(attr_name, NOTHING)`.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: `_transform_attrs` is defined in the unshown `_make.py`.

items.claim: `to_bool` maps the integer `1` to `True` and `0` to `False`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The documented doctest for `to_bool` shows truthy strings converting to True and `0` converting to False, with ints accepted by the stub signature.

items.claim: `asdict` supports a `dict_factory` parameter allowing custom dictionary types such as `OrderedDict`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `asdict` takes a `dict_factory` parameter and the docstring explicitly mentions passing `collections.OrderedDict`.

items.claim: `resolve_types` uses `typing.get_type_hints` and accepts `globalns` and `localns` arguments.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `resolve_types(cls, globalns=None, localns=None, ...)` builds kwargs and calls `typing.get_type_hints`.

items.claim: attrs does not generate a `__ne__`; `add_eq` assigns one shared module-level function.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: A module-level `__ne__` in `_make` is imported by `_cmp.py`, but `add_eq`'s behavior itself is in the unshown `_make.py`.

items.claim: A class cannot use both `frozen=True` and `on_setattr` hooks; doing so raises a `ValueError` with the message "Frozen classes can't use on_setattr."
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: The validation logic and its error message live in src/attr/_make.py, which is not shown; the changelog only notes that frozen classes may set `on_setattr` to `None` or `NO_OP`.

items.claim: `attr.asdict` converts tuples, sets and frozensets to `list` unless `retain_collection_types` is set.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `asdict` picks `cf = value_type if retain_collection_types is True else list` for tuple/list/set/frozenset values.

items.claim: Even in the `these` path, `_transform_attrs` calls `_get_annotations` and uses `anns.get(attr_name)` as each field's type.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: `_transform_attrs`'s handling of the `these` path is in the unshown `_make.py`.

items.claim: `slots_setstate` accepts either a tuple (for pickles written by attrs before v22.2.0) or a dict, and when given a dict sets only the names actually present.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: `slots_setstate` is defined in the unshown `_make.py`.

items.claim: `_determine_whether_to_implement`, given a None flag and `auto_detect=True`, loops over the dunder names calling `_has_own_attribute`.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: `_determine_whether_to_implement` and `_has_own_attribute` live in the unshown `_make.py`.

items.claim: When `auto_attribs=True`, `_transform_attrs` converts PEP 526 annotations into attributes.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: `_transform_attrs` is defined in src/attr/_make.py, whose contents are not shown, so its handling of PEP 526 annotations can't be checked.

items.claim: attrs security issues should be reported via the Tidelift security contact.
items.label: supported
items.reason: SECURITY.md directs vulnerability reports to the Tidelift security contact.

items.claim: When the class has both `__module__` and `__qualname__`, `_ClassBuilder.__init__` sets `self._add_method_dunders = self._add_method_dunders_unsafe`, the variant that assigns without `contextlib.suppress`.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: `_ClassBuilder.__init__` is in the unshown `_make.py`.

items.claim: In `asdict`, a dict value is rebuilt with `dict_factory` over key/value pairs, with keys processed using `is_key=True`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The dict branch of `asdict` builds `df(...)` from `_asdict_anything(kk, is_key=True, ...)` / `_asdict_anything(vv, is_key=False, ...)` pairs.

items.claim: When `init=False`, attrs routes the identical generated script to `__attrs_init__` instead of `__init__`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The docs state that when attrs is told not to write an `__init__` (e.g. `init=False`), it writes `__attrs_init__` with the same code instead.

items.claim: `attr.s` resolves `order` to mirror `eq`, so `make_class` enables ordering by default, while `define` does not.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The docs state *order* is False by default in `attrs.define` but not in `attr.s` (whose `order=None` mirrors `eq`), which `make_class` shares.

items.claim: For a frozen slotted class, `_determine_setters` returns a `_setattr` strategy going through a cached `object.__setattr__`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The docs state that for frozen slotted classes attrs uses an aggressively cached `object.__setattr__` to set attributes.

items.claim: `ClassProps.__init__` takes sixteen positional settings and assigns them directly to slots.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The documented `ClassProps` repr lists exactly sixteen settings from `is_exception` through `field_transformer`.

items.claim: `fields` calls `get_generic_base` to determine whether the argument is a specialized generic.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: `get_generic_base` is shown being used by `has()`, but `fields()` itself is in the unshown `_make.py`.

items.claim: The coverage job in CI runs `coverage combine` followed by `coverage report --fail-under=100`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The coverage job runs `coverage combine` and later `coverage report --fail-under=100`.

items.claim: `tests/test_forward_references.py` is ignored on Python versions below 3.14.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: The only mention of that file sets a ruff per-file target version of py314; whether the test is skipped on older Pythons is in tests/test_forward_references.py, which is not shown.

items.claim: Since version 21.1.0, the `eq` and `order` field parameters also accept custom callables.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The 21.1.0 changelog entry states it's now possible to customize `eq` and `order` behavior by passing in a callable.

items.claim: The attrs AI policy prohibits listing LLM bots in `Co-authored-by` tags.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The AI policy states "No LLM bots in `Co-authored-by:`s" and that such PRs will be closed.

items.claim: `has()` checks whether a class is an `attrs` class.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `has(cls)` is documented and implemented as checking whether a class has attrs attributes.
